final_proof:
As written, two explanatory type annotations are reversed. If \(L:\mathbf D\to\mathbf C\), then \(L^{\mathrm{op}}:\mathbf D^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf C^{\mathrm{op}}\), not \(\mathbf C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf D^{\mathrm{op}}\). Moreover, the ordinary hom bifunctor of \(\mathbf C\) has type
\[
H_{\mathbf C}=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(-,-):\mathbf C^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathbf C\longrightarrow\mathbf{Set}.
\]
Thus, with the displayed erroneous types, the statement is not well-typed. With these necessary corrections, the claimed equality is true.

The product functor
\[
L^{\mathrm{op}}\times\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}:\mathbf D^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathbf C\longrightarrow \mathbf C^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathbf C
\]
is well-defined. Let
\[
K=H_{\mathbf C}\circ(L^{\mathrm{op}}\times\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}).
\]
For an object \((D,X)\) of \(\mathbf D^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathbf C\),
\[
K(D,X)=H_{\mathbf C}(LD,X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(LD,X),
\]
which is exactly the value of \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(L-,-)\) at \((D,X)\).

Now let \((u,v):(D,X)\to(D',X')\) be a morphism in \(\mathbf D^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathbf C\). Thus \(u:D\to D'\) in \(\mathbf D^{\mathrm{op}}\), equivalently \(u^{\mathrm{op}}:D'\to D\) in \(\mathbf D\), while \(v:X\to X'\) in \(\mathbf C\). The morphism
\[
L^{\mathrm{op}}u:LD\to LD'
\]
in \(\mathbf C^{\mathrm{op}}\) corresponds to
\[
L(u^{\mathrm{op}}):LD'\to LD
\]
in \(\mathbf C\). Therefore, by the definition of the ordinary hom bifunctor, the function induced by \(K\) is
\[
K(u,v):\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(LD,X)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(LD',X'),
\qquad f\longmapsto v\circ f\circ L(u^{\mathrm{op}}).
\]
This is precisely the defining action of \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(L-,-)\) on \((u,v)\). Hence the two functors agree on every object and every morphism. Consequently,
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(L-,-)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(-,-)\circ(L^{\mathrm{op}}\times\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}).
\]

Finally, local smallness of \(\mathbf C\) ensures that every \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(LD,X)\) is a set, so both sides indeed take values in \(\mathbf{Set}\). The local smallness of \(\mathbf D\) is not needed for this identity.
